_comment: canon-owned semantic web/UI spec layer. Rule body = intent below (this text IS the rule). Deterministic parts (raw palette classes / inline class scatter / rsx nesting / rsx-per-component / Chinese-in-rsx / import direction) live in the l1 checklists that run dioxus_web.py — do NOT re-judge them here; this config only covers meaning-level rules a grep cannot. Deployed to ferrite/kymido/ui-kit via canon-sync; keep paths portable (no repo-specific layout in this file).

web_spec.intent: Web UI component specification for Dioxus/Rust web code (component crates, page crates, apps that render rsx). Canonical sources: ui-component-principles.md (component creation baseline) and web-code-review-guide.md (readability + refactor discipline), as deployed in the consuming repo's todo/. Rules: (P1 OWNERSHIP) a shared component crate (ui-kit src/, kymido crates/web-ui, ferrite crates/web/ui-components) must never import business types — contract, api client, page DTO, or page state; business semantics in a shared component is an ownership error, move it back to the page. One-off layout compositions stay inline in rsx; only cross-page (>=2 pages) or cross-app reusable primitives get extracted. (P2 OVERLAY MATRIX) single-field editing (price, multiplier, note, toggle) = click-triggered Popover per field; dangerous confirmation or atomic input (delete confirm, paste secret) = modal Dialog; create / multi-field full edit = Sheet drawer; read-only detail = card + tabs; right-click context menus are forbidden; checkbox batch operations are forbidden (batch goes through NL agent). (P3 API) controlled-first: value + on_change; an uncontrolled internal truth source must state the reason; closed style sets use a variant enum, never render_x: bool switch bloat; props <= 7, beyond that split into subcomponents or a parameter object; callback names on_change / on_open_change / on_select, never handle_*; data-fetching components model idle/loading/ready/error explicitly and render each state (busy-poll without a loading state is the documented #230 incident). (P4 VISUALS) colors/radius/typography route through the design token layer; a raw Tailwind shade color utility where a semantic token covers the same role is a violation; state colors are semantically fixed — destructive only for irreversible operations, warning only for recoverable risk. (P5 A11Y) interactive elements carry data-testid (value = name) and containers carry role + aria-label; overlay components implement APG keyboard/focus (Escape closes without submitting, outside click closes, focus trap, focus returns to trigger); icon buttons have an accessible name with the icon aria-hidden; any hover-triggered interaction must also work via click/tap. (G1 DIOXUS ANTI-PATTERNS) no effect that writes a signal it reads (self-loop); no busy-polling to wait for data (model loading); no use_effect doing derived work that should be use_memo; list keys must be stable business ids, never array indexes; event closures must not capture stale values — read current values through signals. (G2 STRUCTURE) page files do not grow past one screen — numbered paragraphs become subcomponents; state ownership is three levels (component-local signal -> page store -> global session/i18n) and state is hoisted only when it crosses pages, never 'just in case'; rsx nesting beyond ~3 levels gets extracted; an if/else-if chain beyond 3 branches becomes match + enum; naming is verb-noun (fetch_channel_models not do_config; signals store data, events are verbs). (G3 REFACTOR TRIGGERS) the same semantic rsx block in 2+ places or a subtree over ~30 lines with a clear boundary extracts into a subcomponent; derived values written via effect become use_memo; long nested boolean expressions in rsx become named functions; repeated condition fragments keep only the diff; props >= 8 collapse into a struct; logic that tests cannot reach moves to pure modules in the page crate. Refactors never change behavior: data-testid, aria role/label, class strings, state branches, button text/order survive byte-for-byte. Judge ONLY from evidence visible in the file or diff; non-component rust, test fixtures, and trivial diffs are no_action.
web_spec.message: web_spec semantic finding: check the question ids in this finding's extras against the intent above; fix the highest-severity one first, keep behavior byte-for-byte.

effect_antipattern.instructions: Does the file or diff contain a Dioxus anti-pattern: an effect that writes a signal it reads (self-loop), busy-polling for data without a loading state, use_effect doing work that use_memo should derive, array-index list keys, or event closures capturing stale values?

criteria.true: One of those five patterns is visible in the code (e.g. `use_effect(|| { ... x.set(...) })` where x is also read in the effect body; a polling loop with no idle/loading/ready/error states; `key: i` or index-derived keys on a data list; a move-closure capturing a value that later changes).
criteria.false: Effects only observe external sources (timers, storage, other components' outputs), derived values use use_memo, list keys are business ids, and closures read through signals or capture immutable owned values.

overlay_matrix.instructions: Does the diff assign the wrong overlay primitive: single-field editing via modal Dialog, a create/multi-field full edit via Popover, a right-click context menu, or checkbox batch operations?

criteria.true: A single-field edit (price/ratio/note/toggle/secret) is implemented as a modal Dialog or full-page form; a dangerous confirm or atomic input uses a Popover; a create-or-multi-field-full-edit uses a Popover instead of a Sheet; or any context-menu / multi-select-batch UI appears.
criteria.false: Single-field edits are click-triggered Popovers, dangerous confirms and atomic inputs are modal Dialogs, create/multi-field edits are Sheet drawers, read-only details are cards/tabs, and no context-menu or checkbox-batch UI is present.

api_contract.instructions: Does a component in the file or diff violate the API discipline: uncontrolled state without a stated reason, render_x boolean switch bloat, callback names like handle_*, or a data-fetching component with no idle/loading/ready/error modeling?

criteria.true: A `handle_*` prop/callback name exists; a `render_something: bool` / `show_something: bool` prop toggles whole UI regions; an uncontrolled internal truth source has no doc comment stating why; or a component fetches data but renders no distinct loading/error/empty states.
criteria.false: value + on_change controlled pattern with any uncontrolled case documented; closed style sets use variant enums; callbacks are on_*; fetching components render each of the four states.

props_bloat.instructions: Does any #[component] in the file or diff take 8 or more props without collapsing them into a parameter struct or splitting subcomponents?

criteria.true: A #[component] declares 8+ #[prop] fields and none is grouped into a struct (e.g. PagerProps-style parameter object).
criteria.false: Every #[component] has 7 or fewer props, or the large flat list is grouped into a named struct prop.

ownership_imports.instructions: Does a shared component crate file import business types (contract records, api client, page DTOs, page stores) — an ownership violation for shared code?

criteria.true: A file in a shared component library (ui-kit src/, kymido crates/web-ui shared parts, ferrite ui-components) has `use` lines pulling in a contract/api/domain type that encodes page or backend semantics.
criteria.false: The file is page-local code (ownership of business types is correct there), or the shared file only imports framework/UI primitives and its own types.

state_ownership.instructions: Does the diff mislayer state: component-private state hoisted to a page/global store, or cross-page state trapped in one component with no documented reason?

criteria.true: A signal that only one component reads/writes lives in a page or global store; or state needed by two pages lives inside a single component without lifting.
criteria.false: Component-local signals stay local, cross-component state lives in the page, cross-page state lives in the global/session layer, and hoisting follows actual use.

rsx_readability.instructions: Does the rsx exceed readability limits: nesting beyond ~3 element levels, an if/else-if chain beyond 3 branches not converted to match + enum, or non-verb-noun naming on functions/signals/events?

criteria.true: A rsx! block nests meaningful elements deeper than ~3 levels; a conditional rendering chain has 4+ if/else-if arms; or a function/event/signal name is not verb-noun (do_config, process_data, channels_data vs fetch_channel_models, on_rename).
criteria.false: Deep subtrees are extracted into named subcomponents, long chains are match arms over an enum, and names follow the verb-noun / data-signal / event-verb convention.

refactor_trigger.instructions: Does the diff keep a known refactor smell that the guide says must be refactored: the same semantic rsx block in 2+ places, a subtree over ~30 lines with a clear boundary, a long nested boolean in rsx, or untestable logic left inside a component?

criteria.true: Two near-identical semantic rsx blocks coexist in the file; a dense 30+-line subtree with an obvious boundary stays inline; a boolean expression nested in rsx is long enough to need a named predicate; or a component body does work (parsing, mapping, api) that a pure module would make testable.
criteria.false: Repeated blocks are already extracted into a subcomponent or shared style constant, dense subtrees are split, long booleans have named functions, and testable logic sits in the page crate's api/pure-function modules.

a11y_gap.instructions: Does the diff leave accessibility gaps: interactive elements without data-testid, containers missing role/aria-label, icon buttons without an accessible name, or hover-only interactions with no click/tap path?

criteria.true: A button/input/select in the diff has no data-testid; a landmark or composite widget lacks role + aria-label; an icon-only button is not aria-hidden-icon + named; or the only trigger for a panel/tooltip/form is :hover.
criteria.false: Interactive elements carry data-testid (value = name), containers carry role + aria-label, icon buttons are accessible, and every hover-triggered interaction also has a click/tap trigger (APG + WCAG 1.4.13).

web_spec_kind.instructions: Classify the primary issue visible in this file and diff. Use mixed when two or more non-trivial categories apply; use no_action when nothing above applies.

criteria.antipattern: A Dioxus effect/loop/key/closure anti-pattern is the main problem.
criteria.overlay: The wrong overlay primitive (matrix P2) is the main problem.
criteria.api: API discipline (controlled/variant/on_*/four-state) is the main problem.
criteria.props: Props bloat without a parameter object.
criteria.ownership: A shared component imports business types.
criteria.state: State is on the wrong layer.
criteria.refactor: An unrefactored repeated block / dense subtree / untestable logic.
criteria.mixed: At least two of the above categories apply.
criteria.no_action: The file satisfies the spec; nothing to change.

web_spec_severity.instructions: How urgent is the spec work this finding points at, for the web-dev lane?
criteria: 0: the file already satisfies the spec; the finding is noise.
1: a local advisory — one naming issue, one missing testid, one extractable block that can wait.
2: the diff creates a real violation now — wrong overlay primitive, business import in shared code, effect self-loop, or state on the wrong layer.
3: the diff introduces a structural violation that blocks merge or changes observable behavior (behavior drift in a 'move-only' refactor, missing four-state on a shipping data path).
